images.title: A diagonal splits each corner into 45° and 45°
images.purpose: Shows square ABCD with diagonal AC cutting the right angles at A and C into two 45° parts each.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large square in the centre with one diagonal and four equal angle arcs.
images.exact_structure: One square ABCD in dark outline, sitting flat, with A top left, B top right, C bottom right and D bottom left. Each side carries one identical short tick mark. A small dark square right angle mark at D and at B. The diagonal AC is a thick teal (#0072B2) line from top left to bottom right. At A two small reddish purple (#CC79A7) arcs, one on each side of the diagonal, each labelled 45°; at C two small reddish purple arcs, one on each side of the diagonal, each labelled 45°. The letters A, B, C, D sit outside their corners. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: In a square, a diagonal cuts each corner it passes through into two 45° angles.
images.description: Shows square ABCD with diagonal AC cutting the right angles at A and C into two 45° parts each.
images.context: ∆ADC: right angle at D, AD = DC, so ∠DAC = ∠DCA = (180 − 90) ÷ 2 = 45.

image_decisions.why: Four equal 45° arcs on one diagonal show the bisecting property at a glance.
